To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of hypertension is a significant risk factor for the development of cardiovascular diseases and that the evaluation of the variations of blood pressure during physical exercise is a valuable tool for the diagnosis, prognosis and treatment of hypertension.

(a) the exercise test is a simple and reliable tool to assess cardiovascular function in hypertensive patients; (b) it is a useful method for the detection of silent myocardial ischemia in hypertensive patients and it is an independent predictor of cardiovascular events in hypertensive patients with coronary heart disease; (c) it is a good method for the assessment of cardiac autonomic function and it is an important tool for the diagnosis of postural hypotension.
exercise blood pressure measurements are useful in the diagnosis and management of hypertensive patients, and that the prognostic value of exercise blood pressure measurement has been demonstrated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the significance and the prognostic values for the various types of exercise blood pressure variations in hypertensive subjects, and with the practical applications of these data.
the prognostic significance of blood pressure measurement during exercise in actual or possible hypertensives, and with its practical applications.
the evaluation of the significance of exercise testing in hypertensives, with the aim of defining a better prognostic value of the test and its diagnostic applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the measurement of blood pressure on effort is a valuable tool in the evaluation of cardiovascular risk and that it should be used in the context of a global evaluation of the cardiovascular risk.
the exercise test is an indispensable part of the diagnostic and prognostic evaluation of hypertension.
exercise blood pressure measurement should be recommended in all hypertensive subjects, particularly those who experience regular significant exercise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exercise test is a valuable tool to be used in hypertensives.
the exercise test in actual and potential hypertensives has diagnostic value and is useful as an additional test in the management of these patients.
the measurement of blood pressure on effort, as well as its evaluation, is of major interest for the diagnosis of hypertensives and for the evaluation of the prognosis of hypertensives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exercise testing is a simple and useful method to assess cardiovascular risk.
the exercise test is a useful diagnostic tool for identifying patients with hypertension who are likely to develop cardiovascular complications.
the prognostic value of exercise blood pressure measurement has now been clearly demonstrated in the hypertensive population.
